personalInfo.name: Karam Matar
personalInfo.title: Software Engineer
personalInfo.bio: Software engineer building backend and full-stack applications with Python, TypeScript and SQL. My work spans satellite-imagery review at Kravi Analytics, an employee survey platform at Softhouse, and dependency-security tooling for Trafikverket.
personalInfo.availableText: Open to full-time roles · Skåne preferred · Open to international relocation

paragraphs: I enjoy taking a practical problem through to working software. At Kravi Analytics, I built the initial version of a Python platform for reviewing satellite imagery, integrating TIFF files from S3. The platform is used across the company. During the internship, I maintained and extended it with a growing focus on backend development. At Softhouse, I contributed full-stack features, security fixes and automated testing in an 11-person team while coordinating customer communication and demonstrations.

I hold a B.Sc. in Software Engineering from BTH and spent an exchange semester at Newcastle University. My systems background includes building a compiler and virtual machine in C++ and mentoring first-year C++ students. For my bachelor's thesis with Iquest AB, I co-developed an autonomous multi-agent bug-fix workflow that creates pull requests for mandatory human review.

I'm based in Örkelljunga and looking for backend or full-stack engineering roles, preferably in Skåne, especially Malmö, and open to international relocation. Outside web development, I enjoy building games in Unity/C# and C++/SFML and studying algorithms through competitive programming. I'm currently learning Blender.

projects.title: TeamTemp — Softhouse
projects.description: Employee survey platform delivered by an 11-person team. I worked full stack throughout, contributed frontend/backend features, testing and security fixes, and served as the permanent Head of Department, team and customer communication contact.
projects.longDescription: An employee survey and engagement platform delivered by an 11-person team at Softhouse, with tasks and features divided among team members. I worked full stack throughout and was the permanent communication contact between the Head of Department, development team and customer. My engineering contributions included configurable scale questions, branch/user role handling, application-security measures, fixes for tester-reported vulnerabilities and Cypress end-to-end tests. I also performed some code reviews, assisted with merge conflicts and helped troubleshoot CI/CD and test integration. The team used unit, integration and end-to-end testing. Separately, I rotated into Scrum Master and Team Lead roles once each; during my Scrum Master sprint I broke requirements into categorized tasks. The team delivery was formally accepted as exceeding customer expectations.

projects.title: C++ Compiler and Virtual Machine
projects.description: Co-developed a C++ compiler and virtual machine for a Java-like language, connecting Flex/Bison parsing and semantic analysis to control-flow graphs, three-address code and executable bytecode.
projects.longDescription: Built jointly with a colleague across investigation, implementation and documentation, this compiler translates a Java-like language into executable bytecode. A Flex scanner and Bison LALR(1) parser construct a syntax tree; C++ visitors build symbol tables, perform semantic checks and lower programs into control-flow graphs and three-address code. A custom bytecode generator and virtual machine complete the pipeline. Graphviz exports make syntax trees and branch/loop structure visible, with example programs demonstrating arithmetic, conditionals, loops and recursive factorial execution.
screenshotCaptions: Syntax tree freshly generated by the compiler for ArithmeticDemo.java, displaying the structure of (2 + 3) * 4.
Control-flow graph freshly generated for C1.java, showing basic blocks, true/false branches and the while-loop back-edge.
Actual generated intermediate code and bytecode for ArithmeticDemo.java, alongside the source and interpreter result of 20.
The freshly built compiler generates bytecode for Factorial.java, then its custom interpreter evaluates 10! and prints 3,628,800.

projects.title: VulnerabilityChecker 2.0
projects.description: Dependency-security tooling developed in a six-person team for Trafikverket. Contributed to PowerShell-to-JavaScript refactoring, database functionality and Windows-based cleanup of entries older than 90 days.
projects.longDescription: A six-person project to modernize dependency-security tooling for Trafikverket, including an Azure DevOps task for vulnerability scanning and JSON SBOM generation. My contributions focused on the shared PowerShell-to-JavaScript refactor, database work and a Windows-based process to automate removal of entries older than 90 days. I also assisted team members with task packaging and CI/CD integration during collaborative development sessions, and kept team members and the Head of Department informed of project developments.

projects.title: ACID Bot — Bachelor Thesis
projects.description: Co-developed an autonomous multi-agent workflow that retrieves bug-fix tasks from ClickUp, implements and tests changes, and creates pull requests for mandatory human review. Bachelor's thesis with Iquest AB.
projects.longDescription: A collaborative B.Sc. thesis with Iquest AB exploring an autonomous multi-agent bug-fix workflow from task intake to pull-request creation. My colleague Abduvohid Ilhomov and I worked together throughout the research, implementation and thesis writing. The workflow retrieves tasks from ClickUp, implements and tests changes, and creates pull requests. Human review and approval are mandatory before merging or deployment. The source code belongs to Iquest AB; the linked thesis is academic documentation.

projects.title: Eshop — Shop and Warehouse
projects.description: Co-developed a full-stack shop and warehouse application with web and CLI interfaces, shared MySQL business logic, and workflows for products, stock, customer orders and fulfilment.
projects.longDescription: Manage a shop's catalogue, customer orders and warehouse fulfilment through an Express/EJS website or a terminal interface. Both interfaces use shared database helpers and MySQL stored procedures, keeping application operations consistent across the two entry points. The relational schema connects products and categories with customers, order rows and shelf inventory. Pick-list operations update stock and order quantities, product triggers record changes, and order status is derived from timestamps. Co-developed with Abduvohid Ilhomov as a database coursework project.

projects.title: FAT File-System Simulator
projects.description: C++ file-system simulator that turns an 8 MiB disk image into files and directories, with FAT allocation, path navigation, access permissions and an interactive command shell.
projects.longDescription: A C++ file-system simulator that connects disk-block allocation to the file and directory operations used in a command shell. The implementation manages an 8 MiB image containing 2048 blocks, with FAT chains locating file contents and directory entries tracking names, sizes, types and permissions. Users can create, read, copy, move, append and remove files, navigate directories and change access flags. Separate FS, Disk and Shell components connect metadata and path handling to block I/O and command dispatch. Built as the main Lab2 project in Operating Systems coursework.
screenshotCaptions: Creating, reading and listing a file in the running Lab2 FAT simulator.
Directory creation and a copied file in the simulator’s root listing.

projects.title: ARMv7 Display Controller
projects.description: ARMv7 assembly controller driving a hexadecimal display through UART commands and push-button interrupts, combining memory-mapped I/O, GIC configuration and register-level event handling.
projects.longDescription: Control a hexadecimal counter from a UART console or push buttons, with values wrapping from 0 through F. The ARMv7 implementation combines foreground UART polling with interrupt-driven button input, both updating shared counter and display routines. Exception vectors, separate supervisor and IRQ stacks, and Generic Interrupt Controller setup establish the execution environment. The interrupt handler preserves registers, clears the input event and acknowledges completion, while a lookup table translates counter values into display segment patterns. An assembly coursework project targeting the DE1-SoC peripheral model used by CPUlator.
screenshotCaptions: The actual CPUlator device panels: UART commands reached hexadecimal A, then a KEY1 press/release advanced the controller to B.
The original ARMv7 controller running in CPUlator after ten UART increment commands, displaying hexadecimal A.
CPUlator paused after the KEY1 press/release, with hexadecimal B on the display and the program’s registers and disassembly visible.

projects.title: Marvin / Shadow — Fake AI Interface
projects.description: A character-driven Python fake AI interface with scripted utilities, backpack commands and country-data exploration, developed across four iterations into a modular terminal application.
projects.longDescription: Meet Shadow, a scripted terminal character that brings numeric utilities, string transformations, backpack commands and country-data exploration into one Python application. Developed across four Marvin iterations, the project grows from menu-based calculations into reusable modules for checksum utilities, acronym generation, inventory operations and data queries. Users can search countries, inspect emissions and population figures, and compare values from bundled datasets for 1990, 2005 and 2017. Menu dispatch, utility functions, inventory state and data processing are separated into modules. The fake AI character is the creative premise of this Python coursework project.
screenshotCaptions: Shadow’s actual menu, including utilities, backpack commands and country-data queries.
The running Marvin 4 application showing an item in its backpack.

projects.title: Terminal Typing Trainer
projects.description: Timed typing practice that compares your transcription against reference text, reports word and character errors, and saves participant scores. Includes difficulty levels and random-character training.
projects.longDescription: Practise typing with reference texts at different difficulty levels, then review word errors, positional character differences, precision and elapsed time. A separate mode provides random-character practice, while file-backed results store participant names, difficulty and scores. The Death Note-themed terminal interface coordinates text selection and practice sessions, with separate modules handling comparisons, timing and result files. Built as a Python coursework application, the project connects interactive input, file processing and text analysis to detailed practice feedback.
screenshotCaptions: The typing trainer’s actual difficulty and practice menu.
Results from an automated demo transcription of the bundled easy text in a disposable local session.
Word-frequency output produced by the standalone analyser for its bundled text.

detailSections.title: Related work: Text File Analyser
detailSections.description: A separate Python coursework application for file statistics: word, character and line counts, ranked word/letter frequencies and percentage reports. It shares text-processing foundations with the trainer while using its own analysis module and entry point.

projects.title: Flask Web Security Projects
projects.description: Two complementary Flask applications covering role-based accounts, encrypted profiles, session controls and authenticator-app login with TOTP.
projects.longDescription: Two separately implemented web-security projects built around Flask, SQLAlchemy, Bcrypt and CSRF-protected forms. Together they explore account management, access control, data protection and multi-step authentication, with a distinct application and workflow for each focus.

detailSections.title: Application security
detailSections.description: An account-management application with registration, password login, admin/moderator/user pages and password-change reauthentication. Bcrypt with a configured pepper handles password hashing; Fernet encrypts profile biographies. Session timeouts, input sanitisation, a Content Security Policy and structured rotating logs bring several security mechanisms into one Flask application.

detailSections.title: MFA authentication
detailSections.description: A separate authentication application combining password verification with QR-based authenticator enrollment and TOTP codes. Session state coordinates setup, while account records track MFA secrets, failed attempts and temporary lockout. The implementation also includes conditional CAPTCHA, configured login rate limiting, a protected dashboard and POST logout.

projects.title: x86-64 Buffered I/O Library
projects.description: An x86-64 assembly library that gives C and assembly programs buffered integer, text and character I/O, with ASCII conversion and explicit cursor management.
projects.longDescription: A buffered terminal I/O library implemented in GNU/AT&T x86-64 assembly and callable from C and assembly programs. Its interface provides buffer loading and flushing, integer parsing and formatting, text and character operations, and cursor accessors. Separate 1024-byte input and output buffers track contents and cursor state, with C-library routines handling terminal reads and writes. The implementation connects function arguments, return values, registers and stack handling to byte-level conversion and formatting. GCC/Make build support and supplied C and assembly drivers accompany the coursework library.
screenshotCaptions: The assembly I/O library called by its supplied C driver, reading five integers and printing their sum.
